look_here_first: Look behind a blue-violet flower at the calyx: a thick white OR dark-violet FELT of short hairs covers it. A purple calyx can still be mealy blue sage. Compare broader, usually serrated stem leaves and condensed upright flower groups with azure sage's narrow nearly entire leaves and more open green-calyxed axis.
project_tracker_diagnostic: rhizomatous clonal perennial; not rosetted; only cauline opposite leaves; linear-lanceolate to lanceolate leaves; calyx densely farinose/mealy; erect repeated verticils

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Wildflower Center printable Hays County native list / NPSOT Hill Country compilation. Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly includes Salvia farinacea. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County detailed treatment.

best_field_traits: not rosetted; only cauline opposite leaves
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey's landscaping frame gives the upright flowering habit and repeated inflorescence architecture at field scale. Use that gestalt only as supporting context; the mealy/farinose calyx remains the decisive field character.
morphology_keys.calyx: UT Texas study: outer calyx densely white-haired or violet-haired, compressed side-to-side, about 5–8 mm long and ~10-ribbed. Not necessarily visibly white!
morphology_keys.morphs: White hairy form often blue flowers/white marks on lip; dark violet hairy form often darker blue without white marks. Both S. farinacea: do NOT use flower/calyx pigment as separate species.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite cauline leaves, blade often ~30–95 × 11–33 mm (occasional 5 mm narrow outliers), lanceolate/ovate, usually serrated; narrower S. azurea often ~4–8 mm wide and mostly entire.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Erect interrupted terminal panicle, condensed paired axillary cymes often 10+ flowers per cyme; many flowers crowded compared with azure sage.
morphology_keys.habit: Rhizomatous clonal perennial with several shoots, typically 30–100 cm in local descriptions; not rosetted.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Salvia azurea: S. farinacea has the characteristic mealy/farinose calyx; S. azurea has a green normally hairy calyx and a taller, more open flowering axis.

curation_status.visual_status: 3 real exact species photos staged; white and violet felted calyx morphs taught, detailed hair macros and arrows remain.

photo_comparison_lesson.memory_rule: MEALY = CALYX with densely packed white OR violet hairs + broader serrate leaves. AZURE = greener ribbed calyx + narrow leaves + airy flowers.
photo_comparison_lesson.look_here_first: Locate the calyx (outer cup behind flower) and decide whether a dense fuzzy coat conceals its green surface; do not confuse dark purple felt with an absence of hairs.

diagnostic_differences.farinacea: Dense white OR violet felted hairs; somewhat flat-sided, ~10-ribbed
diagnostic_differences.azurea: Bell-shaped greener, ~15-ribbed in local var. grandiflora, shorter/sparser hairs
Commonly 4–8 mm wide, entire or nearly so

cautions: Dark violet hairy calyx is also farinacea.
Not every cultivated farinacea represents original local genotype; source photos retain locality.
Do not count individual calyx hairs from wide field photographs.
